children: KFC plans to launch the Open House experimental restaurant this week in McKinney, Texas. The site will serve as a test lab for restaurant design, menu ideas, service models, and technology that could scale across the broader KFC system. The 3,400-square-foot experimental restaurant is the physical centerpiece of the chain's "Kentucky Fried Comeback" in the U.S.

Open House combines fast-food convenience with a more hospitality-driven dine-in experience. In the testing phase, customers can use self-order kiosks, two drive-thru lanes, a dedicated mobile-order lane, and a delivery pickup area, but diners can also sit down and have their food brought to the table. The location adds late-night hours, a photo booth, and branded merchandise, as well as a contemporary, open-concept design intended to make the restaurant feel warmer and more social than a conventional quick-service outlet.

The menu leans into KFC staples while also expanding into new areas such as breakfast and specialty beverages. The store will test KFC Sips beverages, snack-size Go Buckets, new sides, and an expanded range of tenders and sauces.
Of course, parent company Yum! Brands
is also responding to fierce competition in U.S. chicken, where brands such as Chick-fil-A, Popeyes, Raising Cane’s, Wingstop
, and Dave’s Hot Chicken have challenged KFC for fast-food chicken market share.

title: KFC tests new menu items, table service, and breakfast at test lab location
